text:
sec-alert-bot: [ALERT] Suspicious SSO pattern detected for multiple users across tenant 'acme-prod'. High-frequency auth attempts from clustered IPs + cross-region hops within 15m. MFA push failures spiked. Automatic session revocation policy triggered for affected sessions.
Olivia: forwarding. looks like impossible-travel + push fatigue combo. looping @Raj (oncall) and @Linh (IAM).
Raj: saw it—I'm on call. pulling the list now. any customer impact reported yet?
Katie: CS pinged: a few customers reported mass push prompts and some lockouts, nothing escalated yet.
Linh: getting auth logs. initial pattern: accounts receive 3-5 push prompts in <10m, then lockout. IPs cluster to 3 contiguous /24s that map to a proxy cluster. UA shows headless browsers.
Mike: recommend immediate containment: 1) revoke active sessions for impacted accounts, 2) temporarily disable push notifications for tenant-level flows, 3) block offending IP ranges at edge WAF.
Raj: implementing step 1 and 3 now. running: `authctl revoke-sessions --filter \"tenant:acme-prod AND last_ip IN (3.5.120.0/24, 3.5.121.0/24, 3.5.122.0/24)\"`
Raj: firewall rule applied: `edge-block add 3.5.120.0/22 --reason sso-proxy-cluster`
Linh: toggling push backoff policy for tenant to 30s exponential, and temporarily disable push for new sign-ins while we triage. command: `iam update-mfa-policy --tenant acme-prod --push-enabled false`
Olivia: good. also enable verbose audit logs and snapshot KMS activity for the timeframe. @audits-bot can you pull key KMS ops 1h before -> now?
audits-bot: Acknowledged. collecting CloudKMS logs, key usage events for tenant 'acme-prod' between 2026-03-18T09:40:00Z and 2026-03-18T10:40:00Z. uploading bundle to s3://redwood-sec/2187654321/kms-bundle.zip
Raj: quick triage: 42 accounts had active session revokes, 118 accounts had 5+ push failures, 7 with lockout. no obvious password spray. pattern suggests automated client chaining through proxies.
Linh: I checked token issuance: refresh tokens look normal; no token minting from new client IDs. looks like MFA prompt fatigue from repeated SAML assertion retries.
Mike: are any RBAC changes required short-term? e.g., disable service-account-based SSO for integration apps to mitigate abuse vector.
Olivia: yes, temporarily rotate critical service account keys tied to SSO integrations and mark them for audit. also add stricter assertion validation on IdP side.
Linh: took a snapshot of current IdP config and enabled stricter audience checks. filed PR for permanent change: `idp: require aacl >1` (ref #3421).
Raj: containment complete for now. will keep push disabled and edges blocked for 1h, then gradually re-enable if no new hits.
Katie: customer comms draft: short note explaining we're mitigating an unusual sign-in flood affecting MFA prompts, we revoked sessions and applied protections, recommending users re-login if prompted. want me to send?
Olivia: yes — keep it factual, no PII, include mitigation steps and ETA for full restoration (~2h).
Raj: monitoring: set temporary anomaly alerts tighter: MFA push failure rate threshold -> 0.5% per minute, impossible-travel L7 -> page.
Mike: also enabling additional KV cache logging for the runtime so we can correlate token reuse and KV invalidations.
Linh: post-incident actions: 1) update audit logging to include SAML assertion IDs in logs, 2) add rate-limit layer to IdP callback, 3) review KMS ACLs for service accounts.
Olivia: +1. set follow-up ticket: SEC-1258 with actions and owners: Raj -> blocking rules, Linh -> IdP validation + PR, Mike -> runtime logs, Katie -> comms, Olivia -> postmortem writeup.
Raj: moving to monitoring mode. I'll post a short incident summary in #incidents after this thread.
Katie: sending customer note now.
audits-bot: Audit bundle uploaded: s3://redwood-sec/2187654321/audit-logs.zip
Olivia: great work. next: schedule a brown-bag with infra and IAM to walk through changes and ensure no regression to legitimate SSO flows.
Mike: adding a canary test to CI that simulates push storms to ensure circuit breakers fire.
Linh: also adding a one-click rollback for IdP strictness in case of false positives.
Raj: closing operational loop here; will update if anything new.
Olivia: postmortem owners looped. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
